questions.q: For what reason does the psalmist say he loves Yahweh?
questions.a: He loves Yahweh because Yahweh hears him when he cries out to him for help.

questions.q: Why did the psalmist say he felt like he was tied up with cords of death?
questions.a: He was so distressed and full of sorrow that he felt as if he were about to die.
Yahweh guards and protects those who are helpless.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say he will do because Yahweh rescued him?
questions.a: Because Yahweh rescued him, he will live as Yahweh directs him as long he is alive.

questions.q: In what ways did Yahweh rescue the psalmist?
questions.a: Yahweh saved the psalmist from dying, from being sorrowful, and from making bad mistakes.

questions.q: What did the psalmist do even when he was suffering?
questions.a: He continued to trust in Yahweh even when he was suffering.

questions.q: What did the psalmist say he could never repay Yahweh for?
questions.a: The psalmist felt he could never repay Yahweh for all the good things he had done for him.

questions.q: Where does the psalmist say he will fulfill his vows to Yahweh?
questions.a: He will fulfill his vows in the presence of all his people.

questions.q: What is precious in the eyes of Yahweh?
questions.a: It is precious to Yahweh when any of his faithful people die.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say he will offer to Yahweh for taking away his bonds?
questions.a: He says he will pray to Yahweh and offer to him a sacrifice to thank him.

questions.q: Where will the psalmist present his offerings to Yahweh?
questions.a: He will present them in the courtyard outside his temple in Jerusalem in the presence of all the people.

commentary.text: The psalmist declares his love to the Lord.

Verses 1–9 We have many reasons for loving the Lord, but are most affected by his loving-kindness when relieved out of deep distress. When a poor sinner is awakened to a sense of his state, and fears that he must soon sink under the just wrath of God, then he finds trouble and sorrow. But let all such call upon the Lord to deliver their souls, and they will find him gracious and true to his promise. Neither ignorance nor guilt will hinder their salvation, when they put their trust in the Lord. Let us all speak of God as we have found him; and have we ever found him otherwise than just and good? It is of his mercies that we are not consumed. Let those who labour and are heavy laden come to him, that they may find rest to their souls; and if at all drawn from their rest, let them haste to return, remembering how bountifully the Lord has dealt with them. We should deem ourselves bound to walk as in his presence. It is a great mercy to be kept from being swallowed up with over-much sorrow. It is a great mercy for God to hold us by the right hand, so that we are not overcome and overthrown by a temptation. But when we enter the heavenly rest, deliverance from sin and sorrow will be complete; we shall behold the glory of the Lord, and walk in his presence with delight we cannot now conceive.

When troubled, we do best to hold our peace, for we are apt to speak unadvisedly. Yet there may be true faith where there are workings of unbelief; but then faith will prevail; and being humbled for our distrust of God's word, we shall experience his faithfulness to it. What can the pardoned sinner, or what can those who have been delivered from trouble or distress, render to the Lord for his benefits? We cannot in any way profit him. Our best is unworthy of his acceptance; yet we ought to devote ourselves and all we have to his service. I will take the cup of salvation; I will offer the drink-offerings appointed by the law, in token of thankfulness to God, and rejoice in God's goodness to me. I will receive the cup of affliction; that cup, that bitter cup, which is sanctified to the saints, so that to them it is a cup of salvation; it is a means of spiritual health. The cup of consolation; I will receive the benefits God bestows upon me, as from his hand, and taste his love in them, as the portion not only of mine inheritance in the other world, but of my cup in this. Let others serve what masters they will, truly I am thy servant. Two ways men came to be servants. By birth. Lord, I was born in thy house; I am the son of thine handmaid, and therefore thine. It is a great mercy to be children of godly parents. By redemption. Lord, thou hast loosed my bonds, thou hast discharged me from them, therefore I am thy servant. The bonds thou hast loosed shall tie me faster unto thee. Doing good is sacrifice, with which God is well pleased; and this must accompany giving thanks to his name. Why should we offer that to the Lord which cost us nothing? The psalmist will pay his vows now; he will not delay the payment: publicly, not to make a boast, but to show he is not ashamed of God's service, and to invite others to join him. Such are true saints of God, in whose lives and deaths he will be glorified.
